text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a perf/regression spike on prod GPUs this morning on paged-attn workloads. 

maria: Symptoms: tail latency +50% and occasional NaN drops in logs when using fp8 kernels with KV cache warmup. Happens only on long-context (16k) streams.

dan: Any repro or stack?

maria: Repro is flaky but I captured a run. Paste of noisy logs: 
```
[2026-03-17 07:22:10] serve: kernel=flash_attn_fp8_v2 selected
[2026-03-17 07:22:10] runtime: kv_cache_warmup=on batches=3 seq=16384
[2026-03-17 07:22:11] softmax: preexp max=1.2e4 overflow -> NaN
[2026-03-17 07:22:11] fallback: switching kernel -> flash_attn_bf16_fused (slower)
```

oliver: interesting — softmax pre-exp max=1.2e4 suggests scaling/clamping missed. Which quant path? dynamic shared exponent or per-tensor?

maria: fp8-e4m3 per-tensor, with no explicit softmax clamp. We normally rely on safe-kernel math that rescales logits, but looks like this variant isn't doing it when KV cache size gets > X and batching heuristics cause interleaved prefix kernels.

tk: Could be kernel selector bias: we pick fp8 fast path when expected seq_len small, but with KV caching and continuous batching, effective seq_len grows. Kernel selector uses sampled seq distribution from recent N requests — that heuristic might be stale.

dan: Do we have profiler traces? small flame or nvprof snippet?

maria: Yep attached snapshot in the repro run, summarizing hot paths: 
- 60% time in flash_attn_fp8_v2 forward
- 30% time in kv_merge + staging memcpy
- rest in softmax fallback and scheduler stalls

maria: Quick table I logged: 
```
seq_len | batches | kernel_selected             | tail_p95(ms)
1600    | 1       | flash_attn_fp8_v2          | 120
1600    | 4       | flash_attn_fp8_v2          | 125
16384   | 3       | flash_attn_fp8_v2 -> bf16  | 190
16384   | 3       | bf16_fused (forced)        | 140
```

oliver: So forcing bf16 fused avoids NaN and reduces tail over fallback. That points to numerical instability in fp8 kernel on large KV.

sre-jen: Any customer impact? Are requests being throttled?

maria: A few API error spikes (5xx) during the window because fallback didn't complete in time for some fast-path clients. Small but noticeable.

dan: Proposed short-term mitigation: change kernel-selector to prefer bf16_fused if kv_cache_size + expected_seq_len > threshold T, and add softmax preclamp in fp8 path. Can we push a config flag?

tk: I can add a selector rule toggle: runtime.config.attn.selector.kv_safe_threshold = 12k tokens. Start as rollout=false.

maria: And I can prototype preclamp: clamp_logits(max_logit=60) before exp, or use log-sum-exp stable trick. But need to verify it doesn't degrade quality.

oliver: Also add a quick perf microbenchmark: compare fp8_v2 with preclamp vs bf16_fused on 16k workload with cold KV and warm KV. That will show cost tradeoffs.

dan: We should also log the kernel input statistics (max logit, var) as a hist counter to Sentry/metrics so we can detect before NaNs happen. Add a rate-limited metric to avoid high-cardinality.

sre-jen: +1 on metrics. If we can detect rising max_logit we can circuit-break to a safe kernel before errors cascade.

maria: I ran a quick local microbench: preclamp reduced NaN rate to 0/50 runs but added ~2% perf overhead vs raw fp8. bf16_fused is ~30% slower than raw fp8 but stable.

maria: Plan: 
- tk: land selector rule behind runtime flag (canary 10% fleet) — ETA 2 days
- dan: add histogram metric for logits + alert — ETA 1 day
- maria: prototype preclamp + perf tests, PR for review — ETA 1 day
- oliver: run 16k microbench matrix across GPU types and attach numbers — ETA 2 days

dan: Sounds good. For release notes, mark as "kernel selector guardrail for kv-warmup".

oliver: Also add unit tests that simulate incremental KV merging to validate no overflow in fp8 path after clamping.

tk: I'll wire the config and add rollout script. Will ping here when patch lands.

maria: Thanks all — adding repro artifacts to the ticket: INF-4821. If anyone sees >3% NaN or fallback rate, please @maria and tag INF-4821. :pray:

infra-bot: deploy-checklist: canary=0/10 -> when selector flag is enabled, ensure canary passes latency SLO for 24h.

sre-jen: I'll watch canary and set temporary alert change for the selector metric.

dan: One more thing — check batching heuristics: if we detect long-running streams, reduce cross-request batching (lower batch window) to avoid mixing seq distributions that trick the selector. That might slightly increase cost but improve stability.

maria: Great point. I'll add a note to the ticket to evaluate batching window tradeoffs.

maria: Closing loop — will post follow-ups here as benchmarks land.
